To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we were able to identify and quantify endogenous cardiac progenitors in human myocardium.

we were able to detect and quantify the endogenous CD117+ and the CD90+ cells in the heart of healthy and diseased patients and that the CD117+ and/or CD90+ cells might be a part of the local endogenous progenitors.
CD117+ and/or CD90+ cells are present in all biopsied human hearts and are increased in the group of myocarditis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and quantification of CD90+/CD117+ CPC.
the identification and characterization of cardiac progenitor cells in myocardium biopsied from patients with different cardiac diseases.
the identification of local progenitor cells in human heart tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD117 and/or CD90 signals in human heart tissue are significantly elevated in cases of myocarditis, compared to other heart disease groups.
CD117 and CD 90 are expressed in the human heart and that the expression is increased in myocarditis.
CD117 and CD 90 cells are present in human myocardium and their number is increased in patients suffering from myocarditis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD117 and CD117/CD90 cells might be part of a local progenitor cell pool in human heart tissue, which might be involved in the pathogenesis of myocarditis.
CD117+ and/or CD90+ cardiac progenitor cells may play a role in the regeneration of myocarditis.
the heart contains local endogenous progenitors, which are increased in myocarditis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heart has an endogenous mechanism to overcome medical conditions, which is mediated by local progenitor cells.
the CD117+ and the CD90+ cells are part of the endogenous cardiac progenitors.
the CD90+/CD117+ cells are present in all human hearts and are significantly higher in myocarditis.
